Welcome

First, a couple of things worth setting up: your name (added to pages you edit) and, if you'll be syncing with GitHub, your access token. You can always change these later in Settings.

Choose a site

Start with the bundled sample site to explore the app, or clone a real site's repository from GitHub.

Or clone a site from GitHub

Use the HTTPS link (from GitHub's own green "Code" button, the "HTTPS" tab) unless you already know what an SSH key is and have one set up on this machine.

Page date & time

Controls sort order for dated content (like blog posts). Use this instead of typing a date by hand in the text - a badly-formatted date can fail the entire site's build, not just this page.

Rename page

Changes this page's title and web address. Doesn't move it to a different section.

Tags

        

          Every tag in use anywhere on the site. Renaming or deleting a tag
          here changes it on every post that uses it - this is site-wide,
          not the one page you were last editing.

Menu

        

          The site's main navigation, top to bottom is left to right. Link to
          an existing page, or paste a web address for anything else. Whether
          this actually shows up as a menu on the live site depends on the
          theme's own template looping over these entries - not every theme
          does this yet; if your site's nav doesn't reflect a change made
          here, that template is the place to check.

          separate on purpose.

Set up GitHub access first

          

            Reviewing someone's draft needs a personal access token with
            "Pull requests" read and write access - it's what lets you
            leave feedback or approve once you're looking at it, and
            without one you'd get partway in before hitting a wall. Set
            one up in Settings → This installation → GitHub
            sync, then come back here.
          

        

        

          
Open drafts waiting for review

          

            Pulled from GitHub's own list of open pull requests. One that
            gets published or closed elsewhere just stops appearing here
            on the next refresh - the same way it would disappear from
            this list on GitHub itself.
          

          

          

          

            
          

        

      

    

    

      

        
Settings

        

          "This installation" is what's on your computer only, and where
          you'll spend nearly all your time here. "This site" is shared with
          everyone who edits it (committed to its own repo) - you should
          rarely need to touch it, so it sits below, visually set apart.
        

      


      

        

          
          

            
This installation

            
Just this computer. Nothing in this section is shared, committed, or visible to anyone else who edits the site.

          

        


        

          
Appearance

          
Applies immediately, this device only.

          

            
            
          

        


        

          
Preview server

          
          

            Makes the preview reachable from other devices on your network (e.g. a
            phone) instead of only this machine. Restarts the preview if it's
            already running.
          

          

        


        

          
Feature tour

          
          

            A short walkthrough of the sidebar, Preview, and the draft
            indicator. Unchecking this just means it won't show up on its
            own anymore - you can always take it from the (i) button in the
            header.
          

        


        

          
Author

          
          

            Added to a page's contributor list on every save. Leave blank
            to skip attribution entirely.
          

          

            
            
          

        


        

          
Image uploads - your credentials

          

            Personal to this installation - never shared or committed with
            the site.
          


          

          

            
            

            
            

            
            
              
              
            
          

          

            
            
          

        


        

          
GitHub sync

          

            Personal to this installation - never shared or committed with
            the site. Leave the token blank if you already sync over SSH
            (e.g. an SSH key set up on this machine); set one to sync over
            HTTPS instead.
          

          

            A token is also required to look at someone else's draft from
            Local Drafts, even if you use SSH for your own syncing - that
            list comes directly from GitHub's website, which has no SSH
            equivalent.
          


          

          
          

            Create a fine-grained token scoped to just this repository, with
            two permissions: "Contents" read and write (for syncing over
            HTTPS - skip this one if you're using SSH for syncing instead),
            and "Pull requests" read and write (for listing, reviewing,
            approving, and commenting on drafts - needed either way, since
            GitHub's pull request API has no SSH equivalent). From
            GitHub's own token settings help.
          


          
          

            Used only to tell your own pull requests apart from everyone
            else's when reviewing someone else's work.
          


          

            
            
          

        

      


      

        

          
          

            
This site

            
Shared with everyone who edits this site (committed to its own repo) - nothing here should be secret, and changes affect every installation, not just yours. You shouldn't need this often.

          

        


        

          
Inserted image sizes


          

            Web standard
            
            

            High detail
            
            

            Post internal
            
            
          

          

            "Post internal" is for an image meant to float left/right with
            text wrapping around it - small enough that the float actually
            reads as a photo next to a paragraph, not a full-width image.
          

          

            
            
          

        


        

          
Image uploads (Cloudflare R2 bucket)

          

            Which bucket this site uploads shared images to. Each person
            still needs their own credentials (see "This installation") to
            actually use it.
          


          

            
            

            
            
          

          

            Public URL base needs the scheme (starts with "https://" or
            "http://") - this is fetched directly by a browser, not passed
            through the site. If you save without one, "https://" is added
            for you.
          

          

            
            
          

        

      

    

    

      

        
Media

        

          Every shared image - stored locally in static/images/
          or uploaded to your R2 bucket. Images that belong to just one post
          (inserted as "with this page only") aren't shown here; they're
          part of that post and travel with it, so manage them from the
          post itself. From here you can rename an image, edit its alt
          text, or move it between local storage and R2 - each card's
          "…" menu.

Delete unused images?

          undone. Uncheck anything you want to keep.

Alt text

      

      

        

          Alt text lives per usage, in the markdown where the image is
          inserted - not as one property of the file. A shared image used
          on several pages can (and often should) describe itself
          differently in each place.
